analysis:
The change is confined to ClusterPlacementPlanner.swift in the cluster placement library. It adds a per-family override: when layout.tensorParallel.family.choosesFastest is true, the planner ignores policy.tensorParallelFirst and ranks by the speed comparison. For an unmeasured link it prices tensor parallel on ClusterTensorParallelChoice.assumedReduction rather than assumingForcedReduction(). The same substitution is made in evaluate() for the explicit-evaluation path. The changes are at head lines ~425-450 and ~637-643.

Security review: the change alters only placement ranking and the assumed reduction cost. It adds no network, crypto, attestation, authorization, key-handling, file-I/O or data-exposure surface. Admission is unchanged. The load gate, memory fit (`possible`, `hardwareGroup`), `admitsShape` qualification filtering, `requiredTensorShares` and the batch-quote allowance checks in placeable() are untouched. `placeable()` still requires `reduction.keyed || tensorParallelForAssessment`. The conservative assumed reduction goes through `link.assuming(...)`, whose keyed or measured labelling I could not see. I assume it matches `assumingForcedReduction` semantics: the link is labelled assumed and linkCostsMeasured stays false. If `assuming(...)` produced a reduction flagged keyed=false, tensor-parallel candidates would not be placeable outside assessment, which fails closed.

The relevant threat entries (T-041, TB-007 and the A-001 plaintext prompts) concern the prefix cache and inference-engine memory, which this code path does not touch. The change could alter which mode is chosen and so performance or availability. It does not weaken any trust-boundary control and does not turn a provider into an adversary-controlled input. I did not see the definitions of `choosesFastest`, `assumedReduction` and `assuming`. Those are outside the supplied evidence, so I found no concrete issue. The patch excerpt was truncated, but the base and head ranges are consistent with the displayed hunks.
